Q: Trying To Find A batch file A:

How it works

1) Find 7-Zip

Looks for 7z on PATH, then the normal install folders.

where 7z >nul 2>&1 if not errorlevel 1 set "SEVENZ=7z" if not defined SEVENZ if exist "%ProgramFiles%\7-Zip\7z.exe" set "SEVENZ=%ProgramFiles%\7-Zip\7z.exe"

2) Get the root folder

From drag-and-drop / argument, or ask the user.

set "ROOT=%~1" if not defined ROOT set /p "ROOT=Folder: "

3) Confirm the folder exists

if not exist "%ROOT%\" ( echo [ERROR] Folder does not exist: exit /b 1 )

4) Initialize counters

set /a FOUND=0 set /a OK=0 set /a FAIL=0

5) Recursively find every .zip

/r walks the folder tree. For each zip, call a subroutine with:

(1) full zip path

(2) output folder = same path/name without .zip (%%~dpnF)

for /r "%ROOT%" %%F in (*.zip) do ( set /a FOUND+=1 call :extract "%%~fF" "%%~dpnF" )

6) Create the output folder if needed

if not exist "%OUTDIR%" mkdir "%OUTDIR%" 2>nul

7) Extract with 7-Zip

• x = extract • "-o..." = output dir (quotes wrap the whole switch so spaces work) • -y = overwrite without asking

"%SEVENZ%" x "%ZIP%" "-o%OUTDIR%" -y if errorlevel 1 (set /a FAIL+=1) else (set /a OK+=1)

8) Print a summary

echo Zips found: %FOUND%

echo Extracted OK: %OK%

echo Failed: %FAIL%

=====================================================================

Full script

@echo off
setlocal EnableExtensions EnableDelayedExpansion

:: =============================================================================
::  unzip_all_recursive.bat
::
::  Finds EVERY .zip file in a folder AND all subfolders, then extracts each
::  one into a NEW folder next to the zip, with the SAME name as the zip
::  (without ".zip"). Folder structure is preserved.
::
::  Examples:
::    Z:\Folder\Folder1\File1.zip
::      -> extracts into Z:\Folder\Folder1\File1\
::
::    Z:\Folder\Folder1\Folder2\File1.zip
::      -> extracts into Z:\Folder\Folder1\Folder2\File1\
::
::  HOW TO USE (pick one):
::    1) Double-click this file, then type/paste the folder path when asked
::    2) Drag a folder onto this .bat file
::    3) From Command Prompt:
::         unzip_all_recursive.bat "Z:\Folder"
::
::  Optional 2nd argument: /nopause  (skip "Press any key" prompts)
::
::  REQUIREMENTS:
::    7-Zip must be installed (https://www.7-zip.org/)
:: =============================================================================

echo.
echo ============================================
echo   Recursive ZIP extract (via 7-Zip)
echo ============================================
echo.

:: ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
:: 1) Find 7z.exe
:: ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
set "SEVENZ="

where 7z >nul 2>&1
if not errorlevel 1 set "SEVENZ=7z"

if not defined SEVENZ (
    if exist "%ProgramFiles%\7-Zip\7z.exe" set "SEVENZ=%ProgramFiles%\7-Zip\7z.exe"
)

:: ProgramFiles(x86): "(x86)" breaks parenthesized IF blocks — use a temp var
if not defined SEVENZ set "PF86=%ProgramFiles(x86)%"
if not defined SEVENZ if defined PF86 if exist "!PF86!\7-Zip\7z.exe" set "SEVENZ=!PF86!\7-Zip\7z.exe"

if not defined SEVENZ (
    echo [ERROR] Could not find 7-Zip.
    echo.
    echo Install 7-Zip from https://www.7-zip.org/
    echo Or add 7z.exe to your PATH.
    echo.
    if /i not "%~2"=="/nopause" pause
    exit /b 1
)

echo Using 7-Zip: %SEVENZ%
echo.

:: ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
:: 2) Which folder to process?
:: ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
set "ROOT=%~1"

if not defined ROOT (
    echo Type or paste the FULL path of the folder that contains your zips.
    echo Example: Z:\Folder
    echo.
    set /p "ROOT=Folder: "
)

:: Strip accidental quotes
set "ROOT=%ROOT:"=%"

if not defined ROOT (
    echo [ERROR] No folder given.
    if /i not "%~2"=="/nopause" pause
    exit /b 1
)

if not exist "%ROOT%\" (
    echo [ERROR] Folder does not exist:
    echo   %ROOT%
    if /i not "%~2"=="/nopause" pause
    exit /b 1
)

echo Will search for .zip files under:
echo   %ROOT%
echo.
echo Each zip becomes a folder with the same name beside it.
echo Existing extract folders will be reused; files may be overwritten (-y).
echo.

if /i not "%~2"=="/nopause" pause

:: ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
:: 3) Counters
:: ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
set /a FOUND=0
set /a OK=0
set /a FAIL=0

:: ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
:: 4) Walk every .zip (recursive)
::    Use CALL :extract so paths with spaces don't break a parenthesized FOR body.
::
::    %%~fF   = full path of the zip
::    %%~dpnF = drive+path+name WITHOUT .zip extension
:: ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
echo.
echo Searching...
echo.

for /r "%ROOT%" %%F in (*.zip) do (
    set /a FOUND+=1
    call :extract "%%~fF" "%%~dpnF"
)

goto :summary


:: =============================================================================
:: :extract  "%zip%"  "%outdir%"
:: =============================================================================
:extract
set "ZIP=%~1"
set "OUTDIR=%~2"

echo --------------------------------------------
echo ZIP:  %ZIP%
echo OUT:  %OUTDIR%\
echo.

if not exist "%OUTDIR%" mkdir "%OUTDIR%" 2>nul

:: 7-Zip:
::   x  = extract with paths inside the archive
::   "-oDIR" = output folder; quotes wrap the WHOLE switch (required for spaces)
::   -y = overwrite without asking
"%SEVENZ%" x "%ZIP%" "-o%OUTDIR%" -y
if errorlevel 1 (
    echo [FAIL] Could not extract:
    echo        %ZIP%
    set /a FAIL+=1
) else (
    echo [OK] Extracted.
    set /a OK+=1
)
echo.
goto :eof


:: =============================================================================
:summary
:: =============================================================================
echo ============================================
echo Done.
echo   Zips found:     %FOUND%
echo   Extracted OK:   %OK%
echo   Failed:         %FAIL%
echo ============================================
echo.

if %FOUND% equ 0 (
    echo No .zip files were found under that folder.
    echo.
)

if /i not "%~2"=="/nopause" pause
endlocal
exit /b 0

Q: Should I enforce uniqueness on a new user-entered identifier in an existing database in the backend, the database, or both? A:

My suggestion is to use the database constraint as the primary enforcement. In other words, attempt the update, catch the exception if a duplicate error is returned, and report a user-friendly message. This achieve both things: avoid the race condition issue and simplify your code.

Another thought is that eventually, after all your users enter a non-NULL identifier, you could alter the column to be NOT NULL, so the database also enforces that the value is required.

Again, you don't have to return the database error message to the user. In fact I recommend you don't do that. Catch the error in your backend code, check for the type of error, and then report a more appropriate message.

I'd also like to know whether the proposed nullable column + filtered unique non-clustered index is the correct approach for migrating an existing SQL Server database,

I'm not sure I understand what you're asking here. "Migrating" means different things in different contexts. If you mean applying CREATE INDEX or ALTER TABLE changes, then yes, you need to do that.

and whether there are any issues I should consider regarding NVARCHAR, collation/case sensitivity, whitespace, or special characters.

This depends on the identifier strings your column needs to store, and what features you require for searches, comparisons, and sorting. I think this is beyond the scope of this question and you need to ask a new question for these issues.

Q: Can't update single package with go modules A:

If module A requires module B, and your program requires both... You will want to make sure module A requires the correct version of module B. Here's some things I end up doing often to keep everything synchronized how I want it.

To upgrade modules, first enter the repository...

upgrade all modules:

go get -v -u ./...

upgrade a certain module to latest commit:

go get -v -u github.com/user/repo@master

upgrade a certain module to a certain branch:

go get -v -u github.com/user/repo@develop

and then type this at the end:

go mod tidy

commit the changes to your repo, and consider a new tag.

git commit -v -a

git tag v0.0.2

git push origin branch --tags

Then, back to your program repository.. and do the same steps, but make sure your imported modules say the right tags when you run that -v -u command.

And make sure that your go.sum, go.mod files doesn't have extra stuff from old modules.

More info here https://blog.golang.org/publishing-go-modules.

Q: Immediate variable substitution in bash function definition A:

It is not possible for Bash, or any POSIX sh, to do this without eval. But even eval has issues. You could do

myvar=ok
eval "function myfunc { echo $myvar; }"
myfunc
myvar=ko
myfunc

and it would print

ok
ok

The issue with the above approach is that it simply embeds the value of myvar in the string and then parses the result as shell code, so any shell metacharacters in myvar will have unintended effects. For example, this:

myvar="hi >/dev/null"
eval "function myfunc { echo $myvar; }"

means this:

myvar="hi >/dev/null"
function myfunc { echo hi >/dev/null; }

so myfunc never prints anything.

Q: Docker Proxy Setup using environment variable A:

You can check if the environment variable has been exported by typing $(name_of_var). For eg, after running

docker run --env HTTP_PROXY="123.45.21.32" -it ubuntu_latest /bin/bash

type

echo $HTTP_PROXY

It is likely that your DNS server isn't configured. Try

cat /etc/resolv.conf

if you see something like:

nameserver:8.8.8.8

then it's likely that the DNS server is inaccessible behind firewalls. You can pass dns server address along with docker run command like so:

docker run --env HTTP_PROXY="123.45.21.32" --dns=172.10.18.0 -it ubuntu_latest /bin/bash

Q: Tableau 8.2 calculated field with If thens A:

Testing for null is redundant (unnecessary) in this case.

An if condition that references a field with a null value evaluates to false. This is different than, say, Java programming. You don't have to test fields for null values before referencing them in most cases. Helpfully, aggregation functions like min(), max(), sum(), count() etc ignore null values altogether.

Unnecessary null tests make formulas hard to read and can easily hide typos. Assuming you meant the test1 instead of test2 in your second test above, then your calculated field need only state:

if test2 < minimum then
  minimum - test2
elseif test1 < minimum then
  minimum - test1
end

Inox is correct that when you do need to explicitly test for null values, the function to use is isnull(), or in some cases ifnull() or zn().
